period_source: Title and abstract: "Men's status and reproductive success in 33 nonindustrial societies"
derivation_basis: Phylogenetic multilevel meta-analysis of 46 studies across 33 nonindustrial societies classified by subsistence type (forager, horticulturalist, pastoralist, agriculturalist). There is no single country-year window, so the UN TFR replacement-status rule cannot be applied. It indexes the pre-modern target phenomenon by fertility REGIME (pre-transitional, contraception coded absent in the extraction) rather than by calendar date: the constituent ethnographic studies are twentieth-century, not pre-1870. Flagged for human review because regime-based assignment to PM is an analyst judgement, not a TFR computation.

period_source: pdf: "NLSY is a longitudinal survey of a sample of American youth born between 1957-64"; "first interviewed in 1979 and were subsequently aged 45-53 in the 2010 follow up study"
derivation_basis: Cohort born 1957-64, first interviewed 1979, completed fertility observed at the 2010 follow-up. The entire observation window falls after 1965 and therefore inside the review's SDT window. No part of the window overlaps the FDT.

period_source: pdf: "I use seven consecutive waves (1988,1989,1990,1991,1993,1994,1996) of the GSS"
derivation_basis: Seven pooled GSS waves, 1988 through 1996. The paper separately cites a descriptive GSS 1972-2000 correlation, but the estimate extracted here is from the seven analysis waves. Window falls entirely inside the SDT.

study_label: Fieder et al. 2005 (Ethology; U. Vienna employees)
period_source: pdf: "The database of 1 August, 2001, specifying an age range of 30 through 59 yr, yielded a total number of 2693 men and 2073 women"
derivation_basis: Single-date extract of the University of Vienna employee database, 1 August 2001, restricted to ages 30-59. Observation date is 2001; the childbearing of the observed cohorts (born 1942-1971) runs from roughly the mid-1960s to 2001, so the fertility being measured is SDT-era throughout. Window falls entirely inside the SDT.

period_source: pdf: "2014 SIPP Data"; "The 2014 SIPP sample is a multistage stratified sample of 53,070 housing units"
derivation_basis: 2014 SIPP panel, wave 1, respondents aged 18 and over. Observation date 2014, entirely inside the SDT window.
